 or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Senior Citizen Commission will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a Commission meeting or

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Senior Citizen Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed
to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit of
Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We will
be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We wi ll base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  /RWINDALE SENIOR CITIZEN COMMISSION

 Issue:  Policy Related to City Sponsored Event Vendors

Staff Recommendation:

That the Senior Citizen Commission provide input and approve the City Sponsored Event
Vendor Policy.

Background and Analysis:

At the request of City Council, staff was directed to develop a policy for all City sponsored
events to allow vendors and nonprofit organizations to sell items at these events. Key
components in the attached policy include:

  •  The policy guidelines, rules and general information
  •  Approved items to sell
  •  The criteria required to register as a Vendor
  •  The specific special events conducted by the City, where vendors will be
  authorized to sell

The Policy is based on sample policies received from other community service
departments in other cities.

In order for the vendor policy to be advertised for the upcoming December events, the
Policy was presented and approved by the City Council on November 13, 2019. At this
time, it is now necessary for the Commission to review and approve this Policy for the
applicable Senior Center events.

Prepared By/Contact:  Eloise Beltran, Senior Citizen Manager
Phone:  626-430-2268

Attachment(s):
  1. City of Irwindale City Sponsored Event Vendor Policy
  Page 1
   CITY OF IRWINDALE
  CITY SPONSORED EVENT VENDOR POLICY

PURPOSE: To establish uniform guidelines for the participation of vendors during City-
sponsored events to assure their participation is compatible with the community event
and enhances the event within the City of Irwindale. The City intends that all City-
sponsored public events provide a neutral environment free of political advocacy or
religious messages for the enjoyment of both local residents and their families, unless
otherwise expressly stated for a specific event. The City further seeks to generally avoid
imposing political or religious messages upon attendees of City-sponsored events, or
the appearance of City endorsement of any particular political or religious message. The
City also seeks to generally avoid any appearance of sponsorship of, or advocacy for,
any particular political or religious message at City events.

GENERAL POLICY
All nonprofit organizations and vendors (hereby collectively named "vendors") who
participate in City-sponsored events shall comply with following guidelines so as to
assure consistency in their participation .

PROVISIONS
  A. General Guidelines
  1. Vendors must submit an application (Exhibit "A") according to the tri-
  annual Vendor meeting identified in Section B Item 1C. Vendors shall
  further pay all applicable fees comply with insurance requirements, secure
  applicable licenses etc. , as further described below and as required by the
  City department that hosts the event. Such requirements shall be met no
  later than one (1) calendar month prior to the event.

  2. The City Manager shall have the final authority in determining who is
  allowed to participate in the City-sponsored event(s).

  3. The City reserves the right to limit the number of vendors due to space,
  available equipment, and/or the sale of similar items.

  4. Refunds are not issued for no shows or cancellations, unless cancelled at
  least seven (7) days before the event. No refunds are given for lost
  profits, claims of duplicate items, location, or weather. Refunds will only
  be given after such seven (7)-day period if City cancels event.

  5. All vendors must check in with the event coordinator 60 minutes prior to
  the event for location information and any updates or changes.
 6. Vendors may not use megaphone or any other noise making device to
  solicit I advertise their booth at any City event.

7. Vendors will not at any time sub-rent any part of their booth or space to
  another party during the event, doing so may result in immediate
  termination of permit with NO refund and/or forfeiture of participation in
  future City events.

8. All vendors must be set up at least 30 minutes prior to the event start time,
  but not more than 2 hours before event. All vendors are required to
  remain set up until the posted ending time for such event. Vehicles (if
  applicable) must be removed from the event area at least 60 minutes from
  event start time. All vehicles are prohibited from driving on any grass
  areas.

9. Items being sold must be maintained in good taste and appropriate for
  family viewing. City Staff reserves the right to order the removal of any
  item(s) deemed inappropriate, disruptive, hazardous or not listed on a
  vendor's application. Examples of prohibited items include, but are not
  limited to, silly string , cap guns, fake weapons, pornography.

10.Vendors will not be allowed to set up in the City outside of the designated
  event area without written approval from the City Manager or his/her
  designee.

11. Vendors should exercise courtesy and consideration in dealing with the
  public and shall not discriminate against any person based on race , color,
  national origin, religion, sex, gender identity (including gender expression),
  sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, family/parental status,
  income derived from a public assistance program , political beliefs, or
  reprisal or reta liation for prior civil rights activity.

12. Vendors are responsible for the cleanliness of the area they utilize. At the
  co nclusion of the event, all trash should be properly disposed of and if
  utilizing a facility, the facility should be cleaned and left in the condition it
  was in upon arrival.

13. All power requirements are to be requested in detail on the application.
  Requests for power on the day of the event will not be guaranteed. All
  extension cords must be supplied by vendors and must be concealed as
  to not be a tripping hazard , and must be in good working order. Cords
  deemed tripping hazards or unsafe will be removed .
   14. The City of Irwindale is not responsible for any injury sustained by
  vendors, their personnel, or guests and vendors, but participating in the
  event, shall indemnify the City for any damages, claims or actions related
  to any such injury, except those caused by the sole negligence of the City.

  15. Smoking and alcohol is prohibited at any City event. No vendor is to
  smoke in or around their booth space at any time. Doing so will result in
  ejection from the event, with no refund given.

  16.Any dumping of oil , grease, or other products or any removal of City
  property, including, but not limited to, fencing, is grounds for ejection and
  possible forfeiture of participation in future City events.

  17. Selling of items may only take place in your designated booth area and
  using items listed on the application and approved for distribution or sale.

  18.All vendors must vacate their space, including vehicles, within one hour of
  the conclusion of the event. Noncompliance will result in a $50 fine and/or
  forfeiture of participation in future City events.

  19. Detailed instructions for each event will be sent out one week in advance
  by City Staff. Any updates to our rules and guidelines will be included in
  those instructions and will supersede this policy, unless expressly stated
  otherwise in the update.

  20. Vendor shall at all times comply with all applicable laws.

B. Qualifications
  When determining whether a vendor may participate in any City-sponsored
  event, the decision will be based on the criteria described in this Section B.:

  1. The vendor meets the qualifications as defined below:

  a. Vendors
  1. Non Profit Organizations (NPO's) are groups located within the
  City of Irwindale or affiliated with the City of Irwindale (ex. Covina
  Valley Unified School District), whose purpose is other than
  generating profit. Monies raised are not for one person , they are
  for the organization and its mission and goals. Nonprofits must
  possess a 501 (c)3 designation . If fundraising on behalf of a
  nonprofit, a letter on organization letterhead acknowledging the
  fundraiser and including the 501 (c)3 number must be provided
   with the application. Failure to meet this requirement will result in
  automatic denial of the application.

  2. Business vendors are vendors located within the City of Irwindale
  whose purpose is to distribute information or sell items made or
  sold at their respective businesses.

  3. Arts and Crafts vendors are vendors who sell their own
  homemade items (ex. Jewelry, crafts, aprons, scarves, etc.) for
  personal profit. This does NOT include previously used
  items/merchandise or mass-produced items.

  4. Informational vendors are organizations whose sole purpose is to
  distribute literature or giveaways that pertain to thei r respective
  organizations. These vendors include: financial institutions, water
  districts, health care providers, etc.

  b. City of Irwindale Organizations or Programs directly affiliated with the City
  of Irwindale Departments. For example Tiny Tots, Teen Club, Cheer,
  Senior Walking Club, etc.

  c. All Nonprofit or Arts and Craft vendors (or their designated representative)
  who desire to participate as a vendor in designated City event(s) are
  invited to attend an optional vendor meeting . This meeting will be offered
  annually to allow vendo rs the opportunity to discuss the policies in an
  open forum and/or ask questions to the respective Departments in charge
  of the event(s) in which they would like to participate in . Any vendor who
  does not attend the meeting , will be required to sign an affidavit agreeing
  to read and comply with the policies and procedures for all Special Event
  vendors as defined in this document. Meetings will be held at 6:00pm at
  the Dan Diaz Recreation Center Banquet Room, 16053 Calle de Paseo,
  Irwindale, CA 91706 on the 2 nd Tuesday in February.

2. The information or items being sold or distributed must align with the event.

  a. Business vendors must align with the event being held, (i .e. , only
  businesses in the health and safety field may participate in the Health and
  Safety Fair)

  b. Arts and Craft vendors who sell during holiday events, with the exception of
  the 4 th of July, should sell items that directly relate to the theme of the
  event.
   3. No Political or Religious Activities. The City, by hosting events open to the
  public, intends to create a limited public forum . City-sponsored or hosted
  events are not intended to be venues for the expression of political or
  religious messages. The intent of the City in sponsoring public events is
  generally to provide a non-political, non-religious, family-friendly, informative
  and/or entertaining , and non-controversial event environment. For this
  reason, no vendor wishing to engage in a political or religious activity or
  otherwise distribute any political or religious message shall be approved. Nor
  shall any approved vendor be allowed to distribute any political or religious
  materials or information or participate in any political or relig ious activities at a
  City event.

  4. Seniors (50 years or older) who have been Irwindale Residents for 15 years
  or longer and previously participated as vendors at the applicable City event
  shall have priority over new applicants in participating in such City event.

C. Permissible Events
  The City of Irwindale has deemed the following events as permissible vendor
  opportunities:

  1.  Non Profit Food Vendors
  a. Music in the Park (ONLY one nonprofit food vendor will be allowed to
  sell at each event) (Recreation Department)
  b. 4th of July Spectacular (Recreation Department)

  2.  Business Vendors
  a. Health and Safety Fair (Senior Center and Police Department)
  b. Business Expo (Economic Development)
  c. Back to School Event (Recreation Department)
  d. Health Fair (Senior Center)

  3.  Arts and Craft Vendors
  a. Easter Eggstravaganza (Recreation Department)
  b. Vendor Fair (Recreation Department)
  c. Irwindale City Spotlight (Library)
  d. Spring and Holiday Boutique (Senior Center)
  e. 4th of July Spectacular (Recreation Department)
  f. Happy Birthday Irwindale (Recreation Department - no vendors)
  g. Back to School event (Recreation Department)
  h. Ml Fiesta (Recreation Department)
  i. Halloween Spooktacular (Recreation Department)
  j . Veterans Day Ceremony (Administration - no vendors)
  k. Christmas Spectacular (Recreation Department)
   4.  Informational Vendors
  a. Music in the Park (Recreation Department)
  b. Holiday events as needed for grant or research purposes (Recreation
  Department)
  c. National Night Out (Police Department)
  d. Book Festival (Library invite only)

D. Vendor Lottery
  1. Recreation Department Events - Vendor lotteries, if required will be held at
  the Parks and Recreation Commission meetings held in January, May and
  September, applicant need not be present.

  2.  Senior Center Department Events - Vendor lotteries, if required will be held
  at the Senior Center Commission meetings held in January, May and
  September, applicant need not be present.

  3.  All Other City Departments - Vendor lotteries, if required will conducted by
  the City Clerk's office. All applicants will be notified by the City Clerk's office
  ten (10) days prior to the lottery event, applicant need not be present.

  4.  This lottery will designate:

  a. Vendor spot (if we receive more applicants than space allows)
  b. Vendor location

E. Event Site Plans
  Site plans for the events identified in Section C are attached to this policy as
  Exhibit "B". These site plans are subject to change and the most recent site
  plans will be provided to the vendor applicants when the application is released.
